description: A receiver applying the record messages of one sender: the version rule, deletions and tombstones, and its user's own changes; and the relations it holds, resolved across senders (spec/records.md).

vectors.description: the example of records.md, section 9, with a receiver that deletes
the example of records.md, section 9, with a receiver that keeps its user's changes against a deletion
a DELETE of an unchanged record is applied, also by a receiver that keeps changes
a DELETE of an unknown id leaves a tombstone that older and equal versions do not pass
a record its user deleted stays deleted, also beside a later DELETE, and a DATA after it is KEPT
a receiver that tracks changes of the whole record, whole record keep
a receiver that tracks changes of the whole record, whole record take
only the kept values that differ from the message are named
a nested record is one value: the start its user set is kept as a whole
a message that brings the value its user set is applied
ids compare as 128-bit values, whatever the case of their digits
a message that cannot be processed changes nothing
a record keeps its type, also through a tombstone
relations merge per element: the user's addition and removal stay, also when the sender adds the same relation again, and the sender's other changes are taken
an extension of a type the receiver does not know is kept as it came, through local changes and updates
the user's change within an extension of a known type merges field by field with the sender's

vectors.description: a relation names a sender by any key of its set, current or removed, or by null for the holder's sender; a key of the receiver's own set names its own records; a key of no known sender, a refused key among them, a record not held and a tombstone leave it unresolved
a relation by a key the receiver does not know stays unresolved until a chain adds the key to the sender, and stays resolved after the key's removal
the receiver's own link: a relation on its own record to a received record, which shows it as linked from, and a relation of the sender to the receiver's record, by a key of the receiver's set
after two senders join, a key of the second names the sender that stays, and null names the records the second sender brought
